investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would write those values.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or all VM slots occupied), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–143 seconds across all three checks before the eval timeout was reached, preventing any agent lifecycle evidence from being produced. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all VM slots are currently occupied by existing remote agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a narrow scheduling domain; if those 2 nodes are at capacity there is zero fallback.

QUATERNARY — Cluster autoscaler not configured or not permitted to add nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, preventing horizontal scale-out when capacity is exhausted.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T01:48–01:53Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to pod node affinity/selector mismatch. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents agent creation from completing, which in turn prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) from obtaining an orgId, agentId, readyState, or state to satisfy the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader user impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing agent pods, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, so even if VM capacity were freed on the other 4 nodes, they would still be ineligible without a configuration change.

Tertiary — concurrent load or leaked agent pods consuming VM slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not clean up agent pods, the VM resource pool may be depleted by stale allocations rather than active use.

Lower probability — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision a new kata-peerpods-capable node in time: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful' suggest no lower-priority pods exist to evict, which is consistent with autoscaler not having added capacity within the eval window.

The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes — 2 due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — causing the pod to remain Unschedulable for ~135–143 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would write those values.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or all VM slots occupied), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–143 seconds across all three checks before the eval timeout was reached, preventing any agent lifecycle evidence from being produced. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all VM slots are currently occupied by existing remote agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, reducing available capacity over time.
QUATERNARY — Cluster autoscaler not configured or not permitted to add nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, preventing horizontal scale-out when capacity is exhausted.

The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to pod node affinity/selector mismatch. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes — 2 due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — causing the pod to remain Unschedulable for ~135–143 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pods. All three sibling checks show the same error within a ~5-minute window (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, failed-check.message), consistent with sustained pool exhaustion.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or nodes were recently cordoned/labeled differently, the effective capacity is structurally limited even when VM slots are nominally available.

Lower probability — transient node pressure or node NotReady event temporarily reducing schedulable capacity on the 2 kata-eligible nodes; would self-resolve without intervention.
